routes.description: Move from an assumed fundamental reality through the explanatory demand raised by arbitrary limits to a foundation whose power, positive value, and persistence are maximal, or as great as eliminating arbitrariness permits.
routes.successCriteria: Establish a defensible principle favoring explanations of apparently arbitrary limits, show that unexplained or strongly grounded nonmaximal limits cannot remain at the foundation, secure some foundational greatness, and connect the resulting limit-free attributes to God-like perfection.

motionBridge.description: Show that removing arbitrary limits from fundamental reality warrants maximal or minimally arbitrary power, positivity, and persistence sufficient for God-like perfection.

centralBridges.description: Justify treating an unexplained nonmaximal parameter among apparently equivalent alternatives as an explanatory cost calling for a deeper account.
Establish that fundamental reality possesses some greatness or value from which the removal of arbitrary limitation can proceed.
Show that a strong necessitating ground of an arbitrary limit inherits the relevant arbitrariness, preventing imperfection from being hidden in a deeper foundational property.

subsidiaryBridges.description: Explain how the limits principle can retain defeasible, worldview-relative evidential force within holistic theory comparison.
Distinguish strongly necessitating grounding from indeterministic creation and reconcile the route with fixed divine structure or foundational simplicity.

routes.description: Prevent the limits argument from independently reaching God-like perfection by contesting its explanatory defaults, its attribution of greatness to fundamental reality, and its inference from explained limits to maximal attributes.
routes.successCriteria: Show that holistic non-theistic theories may rationally retain fundamental limits, that rival principles create unresolved symmetry, or that the route lacks an independently warranted bridge from a neutral foundation to mentality, value, and perfection.

motionBridge.description: Show that the limits argument leaves God-like perfection underdetermined because its essential explanatory, axiological, or maximality premises require disputed independent support.

centralBridges.description: Establish that explanatory experience yields only a defeasible default whose exceptions may be warranted by a theory's independent simplicity and explanatory success.
Demonstrate that similarly motivated rival causal principles can oppose traditional theism unless a principled symmetry breaker is supplied.
Show that a mindless foundation may be axiologically neutral and that grounding or enabling derivative value need not confer value on its ground.
Preserve the possibility that an essential, necessary, or deeply explained limitation is non-arbitrary while remaining genuinely nonmaximal.

subsidiaryBridges.description: Test whether arbitrariness inheritance can explain grounded limits without also transmitting created limits to their divine explanation.
Require proposed explanations of fixed divine structure to remain compatible with the accompanying account of divine simplicity and fundamentality.

sections.title: Explanatory Status of Arbitrary Limits
sections.rationale: Covers the definition of arbitrariness and the competing accounts of whether explanatory experience and apparently irrelevant alternatives warrant seeking explanations of fundamental limits.

sections.title: Holistic Theory Comparison and Principle Symmetry
sections.rationale: Addresses the argument's defeasible or worldview-relative force, the role of independent theoretical virtues, and the burden of distinguishing the limits principle from rival principles.

sections.title: Foundational Greatness and Value Grounding
sections.rationale: Tests the indispensable move from a potentially mindless or neutral foundation to some positive value through mentality, grounding, productive capacity, or other greatness-conferring features.

sections.title: Explained Limits and Arbitrariness Inheritance
sections.rationale: Examines whether necessary, essential, or strongly grounded nonmaximal limits remain arbitrary and whether arbitrariness can be inherited without overextending to creative explanation.

sections.title: God-Like Perfection and Divine Models
sections.rationale: Covers the completion of the motion-level inference to maximal power, positivity, and persistence together with challenges arising from fixed divine structure, simplicity, and modal extensions.

moves.speaker: Josh Rasmussen
moves.proposition: Arbitrariness inheritance is restricted to strong necessitating grounding and need not extend to indeterministic creative explanations, so a free creator can produce contingent limits without inheriting them.
moves.attributionBasis: Rasmussen answers Schmid by explicitly distinguishing strong necessitating grounding from creative relations involving choice and indeterminacy.

components.text: Whether the inheritance principle illegitimately extends from necessitating grounding to God's contingent creative explanations.

response.rationale: The reply directly distinguishes tight necessitating grounding from indeterministic creative relations involving choice and reasons, denying that the same inheritance intuition applies across them.

responsivenessWithinClass.rationale: It squarely answers the creation counterexample with an explicit relevant difference, though the difference is defended mainly through intuition.

precisionFindings.rationale: The boundary is clearly drawn around strong necessitating grounding, with creative and indeterministic explanation expressly excluded.

calibrationFindings.rationale: The speaker calls the point a confession about differing intuitive pull, appropriately calibrating the limited defense.

charity.alternative: Both grounding and creation are explanatory relations, so arbitrariness might transmit through either.
charity.decisiveQualification: Only the grounding relation under discussion tightly necessitates the one arbitrary outcome, whereas free creation permits alternatives.

logicalCoherence.rationale: The necessity-versus-indeterminacy distinction provides a coherent restriction and answers the direct overextension challenge.

evidenceWarrant.rationale: The distinction is clearly described, but the non-transmission conclusion is supported chiefly by reported intuition rather than a defended theory.

relevanceBurden.rationale: It maximally attacks the subsidiary inheritance-scope objection by supplying the required creative-grounding distinction.

representationalCharity.rationale: The response accepts the shared explanatory role while identifying necessitation and indeterminacy as the decisive proposed difference.

moves.evidenceBasis: The excerpt contrasts creative relations involving reasons and indeterminacy with tight, strong, necessitating grounding where arbitrariness seems to transmit.

moves.speaker: Joe Schmid
moves.proposition: Grounding divine tripersonality in a deeper layer of divine reality may conflict with traditional divine simplicity, so the limits argument must remain coherent with the resulting model of God.
moves.attributionBasis: Schmid announces a final point about models of God and directly develops the divine-simplicity consequence of Rasmussen's grounding response.

components.text: Whether the proposed deeper grounding structure within God remains compatible with traditional divine simplicity and fundamentality.

response.rationale: The reply shifts from creation to an explicit model-coherence consequence, arguing that a deeper divine ground and grounded tripersonality appear to introduce layers within God.

responsivenessWithinClass.rationale: It contacts a material model consequence of the grounding account, although it does not challenge the grounding-versus-creation distinction itself.

precisionFindings.rationale: The objection is carefully restricted to the traditional doctrine of divine simplicity and to a model with deeper divine grounding layers.

calibrationFindings.rationale: The repeated framing as a worry appropriately matches the conceptual tension rather than asserting formal inconsistency.

charity.alternative: Grounding distinctions within God might be compatible with simplicity if they do not constitute separable parts or properties.
charity.decisiveQualification: The model still owes an account of how asymmetric deeper and grounded layers avoid the prohibited complexity.

logicalCoherence.rationale: The apparent tension between internal grounding layers and traditional simplicity is clearly stated, with a bounded doctrinal bridge remaining.

evidenceWarrant.rationale: The conceptual description supports a model cost, but no detailed simplicity account is examined to establish incompatibility.

relevanceBurden.rationale: It directly supports the subsidiary theological-cost bridge by requiring coherence between divine grounding and simplicity.

representationalCharity.rationale: The objection leaves room for sophisticated simplicity models while identifying their exact unresolved explanatory burden.

moves.evidenceBasis: The excerpt worries that grounding tripersonality in a deeper divine layer creates two levels within God and may conflict with traditional simplicity.

moves.speaker: Josh Rasmussen
moves.proposition: Removing arbitrary limits from fundamental reality supports maximal power, positivity, and persistence, or at least the greatest degrees of those attributes compatible with eliminating arbitrariness.
moves.attributionBasis: Rasmussen introduces the three-part picture, applies the arbitrary-limits method to each attribute, and states both perfect and quasi-perfect conclusions.

response.rationale: This constructive culmination applies the anti-arbitrariness method to power, positivity, and persistence and has no reply target under the locked classification.

responsivenessWithinClass.rationale: Within constructive moves, it explicitly states the three attributes and both maximal and qualified least-arbitrary conclusions.

precisionFindings.rationale: The three dimensions are identifiable, and timelessness and greatest-compatible alternatives are expressly included as qualifications.

calibrationFindings.rationale: The least-arbitrary proposal is carefully softened, but maximality still slightly outruns the compressed comparison with nonmaximal structured alternatives.

logicalCoherence.rationale: The triadic conclusion is structured and qualified, but a material bridge remains from reducing arbitrariness to maximal values on each dimension.

evidenceWarrant.rationale: The passage states the least-arbitrary ranking without a developed comparison showing why all principled nonmaximal alternatives fare worse.

relevanceBurden.rationale: It directly completes the stated motion bridge by connecting eliminated arbitrary limits to maximal or least-arbitrary divine attributes.

representationalCharity.rationale: The culminating construction states its positive model without directly assessing a developed rival interpretation.

moves.evidenceBasis: The excerpt identifies maximal power, maximal persistence or timelessness, and maximal positivity, then offers a gentler arbitrariness-reduction formulation.
